newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia May palm oil output up 6.4 pct-Ivan Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia May palm oil output up 6.4 pct-Ivan Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in May was estimated to have risen by 6.4 percent to 780,000 tonnes over April, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Friday.
Wong had earlier projected an increase of 7.0 percent to 784,000 tonnes.

Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of May at 740,000 tonnes, compared with his earlier estimates of 745,000 tonnes and the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 697,714 tonnes at end-April.
Wong maintained his earlier estimates of palm oil exports in May at 635,000 tonnes against 570,067 tonnes in April.
In a report, Wong said with the exception of three large producers which posted double-digit increases, the majority recorded gains of five to seven percent in output.
He said the five-week dry spell in the country has been broken since last week with good rains reported in most crop areas. "We thus expect a pickup in production from next week onwards," he said.
Wong said the modest increase in exports reflected growth in offtake by India and Pakistan.
"At this moment, we still do not expect exports this month to be better than May," he said.
Malaysia palm oil supply-demand estimate/projection as of June 13, 1997. (All figures in '000 tonnes)
